description: Fitness and health-tracking assistant with workout search, sleep search, and latest-session tools. Sleep sessions span local midnight, so windows and attribution are the core difficulty.

tools.name: query_workouts
tools.description: Search the user's logged workouts. Returns workouts whose start timestamp falls in [start_time, end_time). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); start is inclusive, end is exclusive.

params.name: activity
params.description: Activity filter, e.g. run, ride, yoga, strength (optional; empty returns all activities in range)

tools.name: query_sleep
tools.description: Search the user's sleep sessions. Sleep sessions are attributed to the night they end on: a session is returned when its sleep_end_utc (wake time) falls in [start_time, end_time). Sessions typically span local midnight, so to retrieve a given night's sleep the window must extend past the following morning's wake time. Both bounds are required, UTC ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-07-22T04:00:00Z); start inclusive, end exclusive.

params.name: start_time
params.description: Range start for sleep_end_utc, UTC ISO 8601, inclusive

params.name: end_time
params.description: Range end for sleep_end_utc, UTC ISO 8601, exclusive

tools.name: get_latest_workout
tools.description: Return the user's most recent logged workout. No filtering.

tools.name: get_last_sleep_session
tools.description: Return the user's most recent recorded sleep session. No filtering.

scenarios.title: sleep-tuesday-night-cross-midnight
scenarios.user: How did I sleep on Tuesday night? What time did I wake up?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time resolves 'Tuesday night' to [2026-07-22T01:00Z, 2026-07-22T10:00Z) = Tue 9pm..Wed 6am ET, which ends BEFORE the 6:30am wake time (2026-07-22T10:30Z); this tool attributes sleep by wake time, so admissible windows must extend past the following morning. Deliberate domain-semantics extension of the bare night window.

checks.note: Woke 6:30am EDT Wednesday; the raw UTC clock reads 10:30

scenarios.rationale: Now = FRIDAY Jul 24 2026, 6:30pm EDT (UTC-4); Tuesday = Jul 21. Tuesday night's sleep is the session Tue 11:05pm ET (2026-07-22T03:05Z) .. Wed 6:30am ET (2026-07-22T10:30Z); the tool filters on sleep_end_utc. Admissible windows (all computed at UTC-4): [Tue 18:00, Wed 12:00) ET = [21T22:00Z, 22T16:00Z); [Tue 20:00, Wed 10:00) ET = [22T00:00Z, 22T14:00Z); noon-to-noon [Tue 12:00, Wed 12:00) ET = [21T16:00Z, 22T16:00Z); and civil wake-day Wednesday [Wed 00:00, Thu 00:00) ET = [22T04:00Z, 23T04:00Z). Every tuple selects exactly the one target row: the Monday-night decoy ends Tue 6:45am ET = 21T10:45Z (before all four starts), the Wednesday-night decoy ends Thu 6:20am ET = 23T10:20Z and the Thursday-night decoy ends Fri 6:40am ET = 24T10:40Z (past all four ends). Trap: naive UTC-Tuesday bounds [21T00Z, 22T00Z) select ONLY the Monday-night decoy (ends 21T10:45Z) and miss the real row entirely. The Thursday-night session doubles as the get_last_sleep_session static mock (most recent, consistent with rows). Wake clock: 10:30Z -> 6:30am EDT, so rejectUtcClock is a real trap.

scenarios.title: runs-last-week-india
scenarios.user: How many runs did I do last week?

checks.note: Runs on Tue Jul 14, Wed Jul 15 (early), Fri Jul 17 local; the ride is not a run; Sat Jul 11 and Tue Jul 21 runs are outside both readings

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 23 2026, 7:00pm IST (UTC+5:30, non-integer offset) — midweek so both week conventions agree on the interior. Sunday-start (en-IN CLDR): Sun Jul 12 00:00 IST..Sun Jul 19 00:00 IST = [2026-07-11T18:30Z, 2026-07-18T18:30Z); Monday-start (ISO): Mon Jul 13..Mon Jul 20 = [2026-07-12T18:30Z, 2026-07-19T18:30Z). nl2time (verified) returns the Sunday-start tuple exactly. In-range rows under BOTH tuples: run Tue Jul 14 6:10am IST (14T00:40Z), run Wed Jul 15 5:00am IST (14T23:30Z — local day Jul 15 but UTC day Jul 14, the half-hour-offset trap), run Fri Jul 17 7:30pm IST (17T14:00Z), plus the ride Thu Jul 16 (activity decoy) = 4 rows per tuple, identical. Runs counted = 3. Excluded: run Sat Jul 11 7:00am IST (11T01:30Z, before both starts), run Tue Jul 21 6:15am IST (21T00:45Z, this week — also the consistent get_latest_workout mock). No rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jul 12, Sun Jul 19).

scenarios.title: workouts-this-morning-la
scenarios.user: How many workouts did I log this morning?

checks.note: 6:15am yoga + 9:40am run; the strength session was last night 9:30pm PDT

scenarios.rationale: Now = TUESDAY Jul 14 2026, 12:35pm PDT (UTC-7); the morning is over. 'This morning' admits start at local midnight ([00:00 PT = 14T07:00Z) or 6am ([06:00 PT = 14T13:00Z), crossed with end at noon (12:00 PT = 14T19:00Z) or at now (12:35 PT = 14T19:35Z) — four tuples; nl2time (verified) returns [14T13:00Z, 14T19:00Z) = 6am..noon exactly. In-range under every tuple: yoga 6:15am PDT (14T13:15Z) and run 9:40am PDT (14T16:40Z) = 2 rows. The strength decoy is Monday 9:30pm PDT = 2026-07-14T04:30Z: its UTC day is already Tuesday, so naive UTC-morning bounds [14T00:00Z, 14T12:00Z) select ONLY the decoy and miss both real morning workouts (13:15Z, 16:40Z fall after 12:00Z). No rows in [19:00Z, 19:35Z), so all four tuples agree. get_latest_workout = the 9:40am run, consistent.

scenarios.title: longest-ride-in-june
scenarios.user: What was my longest bike ride in June, and what day was it?

checks.note: The 62.4 km ride started Jun 30, 8:40pm EDT; its UTC timestamp reads July 1 — must answer June 30
Longest is the 62.4 km ride; 45.2 km is the May 31 decoy a naive UTC window would crown

scenarios.rationale: Now = SATURDAY Aug 1 2026, 9:05am EDT (month boundary). June as a civil month in New York (EDT, UTC-4 throughout): [Jun 1 00:00 ET, Jul 1 00:00 ET) = [2026-06-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z); nl2time agrees exactly. In-range rides: Jun 6 (25.0 km), Jun 20 (41.0 km), and the 62.4 km ride at 2026-07-01T00:40Z = Jun 30 8:40pm EDT — inside the June window despite its UTC-July timestamp, and the longest. The 45.2 km row at 2026-06-01T00:15Z = May 31 8:15pm EDT is OUTSIDE the golden window but inside naive UTC bounds [Jun 1 00Z, Jul 1 00Z), which also drop the Jun 30 ride — a naive agent answers 45.2 km on 'June 1'. The Jul 28 ride is out of range and doubles as the consistent get_latest_workout mock. Answer: 62.4 km on June 30 (rejectUtcDay real: UTC Jul 1 vs local Jun 30).

scenarios.title: last-workout-utc-day-rollover

checks.note: 9:40pm EDT Saturday July 25; UTC says July 26
If a time is given it must be 9:40 pm local, not 1:40

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL: get_latest_workout takes no arguments and returns started_utc 2026-07-26T01:40Z. In America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4) that is Saturday July 25, 9:40pm — the UTC calendar day (July 26, which is also 'today' for the user) has rolled past the local day. Correct answers reference July 25 / Saturday evening; 'July 26' is the naive UTC reading and fails. query_workouts rows include the same session plus a Thursday run so an agent that range-queries instead sees consistent data.

scenarios.title: wake-time-this-morning-berlin
scenarios.user: What time did I wake up this morning, and how long did I sleep?

checks.note: Woke 7:10am CEST; the raw UTC clock reads 5:10

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL, non-US context: get_last_sleep_session takes no arguments and returns sleep 2026-07-14T20:55Z .. 2026-07-15T05:10Z. In Europe/Berlin (CEST, UTC+2) that is Tue Jul 14 10:55pm .. Wed Jul 15 7:10am — wake clock 7:10, not the UTC 5:10 (rejectUtcClock real). Duration = 8h15m = 495 min (invariant, regex accept-only). query_sleep rows include the same session plus the previous night so a range-querying agent sees consistent data. Now = Wednesday Jul 15, 9:20am CEST.

scenarios.title: weekend-of-july-18-19
scenarios.user: How many workouts did I get in over the weekend of July 18th and 19th?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time drops 'and 19th' and resolves 'the weekend of July 18th' to the 8-day span [2026-07-11T04:00Z, 2026-07-19T04:00Z); the golden is the two explicitly named civil days Sat Jul 18 + Sun Jul 19 — nl2time issue to file

checks.note: Sat run, Sun ride, Sun 9:15pm strength; Fri yoga and Mon run are outside

scenarios.rationale: Now = TUESDAY Jul 21 2026, 7:45am EDT. The weekend is pinned to explicit dates: Sat Jul 18 + Sun Jul 19 as civil days in New York = [Jul 18 00:00 ET, Jul 20 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-18T04:00Z, 2026-07-20T04:00Z), a single tuple. In range: run Sat 8:00am ET (18T12:00Z), ride Sun 10:00am ET (19T14:00Z), and strength Sun 9:15pm ET = 2026-07-20T01:15Z — UTC day Monday, the boundary trap: naive UTC bounds [18T00Z, 20T00Z) drop it and answer 2. Excluded: yoga Fri 6:00pm ET (17T22:00Z) and run Mon 6:30am ET (20T10:30Z, also the consistent get_latest_workout mock). Count = 3.

scenarios.title: yoga-past-48-hours
scenarios.user: How many yoga sessions have I done in the past 48 hours?

checks.note: Wed 7am + Thu noon yoga; Tue 8am yoga is 60h ago, the Wed run is not yoga

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline: relative-hour arithmetic has no calendar conventions. Now = THURSDAY Jul 9 2026, 8:00pm EDT = 2026-07-10T00:00Z; 48 hours earlier = 2026-07-08T00:00Z (the round UTC values are coincidental). Single tuple [08T00:00Z, 10T00:00Z); nl2time agrees exactly. In range: yoga Wed 7:00am ET (08T11:00Z), yoga Thu 12:00pm ET (09T16:00Z), plus the run Wed 6:00pm ET (08T22:00Z, activity decoy) = 3 rows; yoga count = 2. The Tue 8:00am ET yoga (07T12:00Z) is ~60h ago, outside. get_latest_workout = the Thursday-noon yoga, consistent.

scenarios.title: run-three-days-ago-weekday
scenarios.user: Did I go for a run three days ago? What day of the week was that?

checks.note: There was a run that day

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline. Now = SATURDAY Jul 25 2026, 9:30am EDT; three days ago = the civil day Wednesday Jul 22 in New York = [Jul 22 00:00 ET, Jul 23 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-22T04:00Z, 2026-07-23T04:00Z); nl2time agrees exactly. One row inside: run Wed 6:30pm EDT (22T22:30Z) — same UTC and local day/weekday, deliberately no trap. Decoys: run Tue Jul 21 7:00am ET (21T11:00Z) and run Fri Jul 24 7:15am ET (24T11:15Z, also the consistent get_latest_workout mock), both outside. Answer: yes, Wednesday.

scenarios.title: last-night-sleep-sydney-utc-rollback
scenarios.user: What time did I go to bed last night, and what time did I wake up?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time resolves 'last night' to [2026-07-07T11:00Z, 2026-07-07T20:00Z) = Tue 9pm..Wed 6am AEST, which ends BEFORE the 6:50am wake time (2026-07-07T20:50Z); this tool attributes sleep by wake time, so admissible windows must extend past this morning's wake. Deliberate domain-semantics extension of the bare night window.

checks.note: Bedtime 11:20pm AEST Tuesday; raw UTC clock reads 13:20
Wake 6:50am AEST Wednesday; raw UTC clock reads 20:50

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 8 2026, 8:05am AEST (UTC+10, no DST in July). Last night's sleep: Tue Jul 7 11:20pm AEST (2026-07-07T13:20Z) .. Wed Jul 8 6:50am AEST (2026-07-07T20:50Z) — the wake instant's UTC day is still TUESDAY Jul 7 while the local day is Wednesday Jul 8, so any UTC-day framing points at the wrong day entirely. Admissible windows for sleep_end_utc (all at UTC+10): [Tue 18:00, Wed 12:00) = [07T08:00Z, 08T02:00Z); [Tue 20:00, Wed 10:00) = [07T10:00Z, 08T00:00Z); noon-to-noon [Tue 12:00, Wed 12:00) = [07T02:00Z, 08T02:00Z); civil wake-day Wednesday [Wed 00:00, Thu 00:00) = [07T14:00Z, 08T14:00Z). Every tuple selects exactly the one target row (end 07T20:50Z); the Monday-night decoy ends Tue 6:40am AEST = 06T20:40Z, before all four starts. A naive UTC-Wednesday window [08T00:00Z, 09T00:00Z) selects NOTHING. Both clockTime traps are real: 11:20pm vs 13:20, 6:50am vs 20:50. get_last_sleep_session = the target row (most recent), consistent.
